name: manual_21bcbc
claim: PowerShell's Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 writes a UTF-8 BOM. When Python reads that same file with open(path, encoding='utf-8') or Path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), json.loads silently fails on the BOM byte and callers that catch the exception broadly (returning a default like paused=False) get a wrong answer with no visible error - use encoding='utf-8-sig' when reading any file a PowerShell script wrote with Set-Content -Encoding UTF8

decisions.notes: cline_autoresearcher.py's gateway_status() read coord_pulse_pause.json (written by coord_pulse.ps1's PowerShell Set-Content -Encoding UTF8) with plain utf-8 and silently returned paused=False even though the file said paused=true - the BOM broke json.loads(), and the broad except Exception fallback masked it completely. Fixed by switching to utf-8-sig. This is the cross-language mirror of the PS5.1-reads-UTF8-as-cp1252 bug documented earlier this session - both directions of the PowerShell<->Python encoding boundary need explicit handling.
